subject: FastPath tail-latency constraints and capacity recommendation
messages:
From: Jane Liu <jane.liu@fastpath.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — FastPath throughput & latency

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side: we want to support an interactive search experience where median response time should be below ~40ms and the 99th percentile should not exceed 120ms for user-facing requests. Typical prompt size is ~350 tokens; expected average QPS during a business hour is ~120, with burst capability up to 500 qps for a few minutes during campaigns.

I've attached a small sample of our QPS profile for last week (fastpath_qps_sample.csv) and our internal tail-latency SLA doc (tail_latency_sla.pdf).

Two asks to help us decide which deployment path to take (Hosted API vs Reserved/Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC):
- Can Redwood meet the 99p <= 120ms target for 350-token prompts at sustained 120 qps and burst to 500 qps without degrading median latency?
- If not, what Dedicated sizing would you recommend (rough order of machines/pods) and what lead time is required for reservation?

We'd like a short recommendation and a pilot proposal by Friday so we can present to our infra team.

Thanks,
Jane Liu
Head of Engineering — FastPath Commerce

Attachments: fastpath_qps_sample.csv (csv), tail_latency_sla.pdf (pdf)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@fastpath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — FastPath throughput & latency

Jane — thanks for the profile and the clear SLA. We're aligned on the ask. A few clarifying questions so we can give a concrete recommendation:

1) Tail definition: is the 99th percentile measured at the token level or end-to-end response (including network and client processing)? For our sizing we assume server-side completion time (server-side model + token decode).
2) Burst shape: you mentioned "a few minutes" — can you share the typical burst duration distribution (e.g., 1–3 min, 5–10 min)? The shape affects whether caching and short-term burst capacity are sufficient.
3) Tokenization: are most prompts ~350 input tokens plus ~50-150 tokens generated, or do you expect longer completions?

Prelim proposal (high level):
- Hosted API (recommended first-pass): With edge routing + prefix cache and continuous batching tuned for your prompt mix, we can usually meet medians and mid-percentiles at ~120 qps. For 99p <= 120ms at 350 tokens, we need to validate with a short benchmark (we run a 2-hour test that mirrors your CSV bursts).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): if you need guaranteed 99p at sustained heavy bursts (500 qps for minutes) with no risk of noisy neighbor variability, Dedicated reserved pools with autoscale buffer are recommended. Dedicated also helps for on-premise data controls if needed.

I'll ask Ben for a quick sizing sketch based on the CSV. If we can get answers to the three questions above today, we can put together a 1-page pilot plan + estimated cost by EOD Friday.

Proposed next steps:
- FastPath: confirm answers to the 3 clarifying questions + share any post-processing latency we should include
- Redwood: run profiling on the sample CSV and hand back a Hosted vs Dedicated recommendation + pilot plan

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Jane Liu <jane.liu@fastpath.com>
Date: 2028-03-23 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — FastPath throughput & latency

Jane/Chloe — I pulled the CSV and ran a quick profile against a representative LLM configuration (350 input tokens + 80 token generation). Notes below (preliminary, bench VM emulated):

- Sustained 120 qps: Hosted API with continuous batching + KV prefix cache should be able to meet median ~35–45ms and 95p in range 60–85ms. 99p at this sustained level is borderline depending on sequence length variance and padding; we'd like a short benchmark to be sure.
- Burst to 500 qps (2–4 minutes): two paths:
  * Hosted: tolerate bursts using autoscaling + burst buffer — you may see 99p spikes beyond 120ms for short windows unless we enable heavier aggregation or temporary prioritized routing (higher-cost nodes).
  * Dedicated: reserve capacity sized to handle 500 qps headroom: approximate starting point = 3 reserved inference shards with 20% autoscale buffer; that mapping equates to ~3 reserved pods in our Dedicated pool (we'll finalize exact vGPU counts after full bench).

Prelim sizing estimate (for discussion):
- Pilot Dedicated: 3 reserved shards (sufficient to sustain 500 qps with 99p ~ under 140ms per our microbench). To push 99p under 120ms at firm SLA, we should consider either adding one more shard or enabling higher-priority scheduling for user-facing routes.
- Hosted Pilot: 1 dedicated priority route + cache tuned; cost-effective, faster to start, but requires agreed pilot acceptance criteria for 99p windowing and fallback policy for spikes.

I'll prepare a short bench plan (scripts + target load) once Chloe confirms the burst-duration distribution.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@fastpath.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-24 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — FastPath throughput & latency

Thanks all — quick leadership note and proposed action items from Redwood's side.

Summary decision path:
- If FastPath needs contractual 99p <= 120ms for sustained bursts (500 qps), recommend Reserved/Dedicated pilot scoped to the sizing Ben sketched, with a short (2-week) SLA beta and a rollback to Hosted if we observe regression patterns.
- If FastPath can accept short, infrequent 99p excursions during short bursts (<=5 minutes) then Hosted API with a priority route and caching approach is the fastest path (no procurement lead-time).

Action items / timeline:
1) FastPath: provide answers to Chloe's 3 clarifying questions + confirm typical burst durations (expected by EOD 2028-03-24).
2) FastPath: share a sanitized 1-week load trace (if available) and confirm any data residency requirements for a Private deployment.
3) Redwood: Ben + Chloe will produce a 1-page pilot plan (bench steps, success criteria for 99p) and an estimated cost/lead-time for Dedicated (deliverable: 2028-03-29).
4) Commercial: if Dedicated is chosen, we'll circulate a short-term pilot SOW and MSA addendum for signature (target: sign within 2 business days of quote).

Please confirm the next call cadence — proposing a 30-minute sync early next week after your responses. Happy to move faster if you want the bench started sooner.

Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions & GTM — Redwood Inference
